title: Platelet count–volume coupling does not improve cross-cycle HbA1c prediction over additive blood indices
abstract: Nonlinear platelet count-volume coupling did not improve frozen 2007-08 to 2009-10 NHANES HbA1c prediction beyond additive platelet/red-cell indices and metabolic risk factors: target weighted MSE gain -0.002032 percentage-points squared (conditional 95% stratified-PSU bootstrap interval -0.003954 to 0.000045; n=5,457). This is a negative representation-specific temporal transfer test, not evidence that all platelet information is uninformative. Target RMSE was 0.779748 versus 0.781050 HbA1c percentage points. Source cross-validation and a serum-glucose-adjusted sensitivity also showed no improvement. Separate survey samples provide within-platform temporal validation only; the interval allows a small benefit.
